Garten of Banban
GAR-tun uv BAN-ban
proper noun (Gen Alpha slang)
Garten of Banban, a horror video game by the studio Euphoric Brothers, first chapter released in January 2023, with many chapters since. The player searches an abandoned kindergarten (German Garten, garden, from Kindergarten) whose giant mascots — Banban, Banbaleena, Jumbo Josh, Opila Bird, Stinger Flynn — have become monsters. Widely seen as an imitator of Poppy Playtime, it spread through YouTube playthroughs and meme compilations and became a Gen Alpha staple of toys, fan cartoons, and recess role-play.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

Garten of Banban is a horror game set in a creepy kindergarten whose cartoon mascots are monsters. Gen Alpha kids know Jumbo Josh and Opila Bird from videos and toys and sometimes play "Banban" at recess. The Christian observation: the kindergarten — literally "children’s garden" — is supposed to be a place of nurture, where little ones are taught and protected. God tells fathers to make the whole of life that kind of garden: teach His words "when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up" (Deu 6:7). "Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it" (Pro 22:6). Children are "an heritage of the LORD" (Psa 127:3). Garten of Banban turns the children’s garden into a hunting ground. Isaiah’s vision of the coming kingdom runs the other way: "the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb... and a little child shall lead them" (Isa 11:6). In Christ’s kingdom the monsters become gentle, and the child is safe. A father can tell a five-year-old: "That’s a pretend school with scary mascots. Real school and church and home are places where grown-ups keep you safe — and God is the One who keeps us all."

Webster 1828 Definition

Kindergarten horror game (2023) of monstrous mascots — the "children’s garden" of nurture turned into a hunting ground, against Scripture’s picture of the safe child of the kingdom.

GARTEN OF BANBAN, proper n. (horror video game, Euphoric Brothers, 2023–present; Gen Alpha usage) The abandoned-kindergarten mascot horror series. "Jumbo Josh is my favorite in Garten of Banban."

Characters in kid lore: Banban, Banbaleena, Jumbo Josh, Opila Bird, Stinger Flynn, Nabnab.

Decode for parents: lower-budget than Poppy Playtime but the same design — school-mascot cuteness made into menace.

Webster 1828, the root — GARDEN, n. A piece of ground appropriated to the cultivation of herbs, or plants, fruits and flowers; usually near a mansion-house.

Key Scripture

Deu 6:7 — "And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up."

Pro 22:6 — "Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it."

Psa 127:3 — "Lo, children are an heritage of the LORD: and the fruit of the womb is his reward."

Isa 11:6 — "The wolf also shall dwell with the lamb, and the leopard shall lie down with the kid; and the calf and the young lion and the fatling together; and a little child shall lead them."

Modern Corruption

Garten of Banban turns the children’s garden into a place of predators; Scripture makes all of a child’s life a garden of teaching and promises a kingdom where the little child leads the tamed beasts.

expand to see more

Mascot horror is a genre built for one audience: children young enough to love mascots. Its pleasure is the shiver of seeing the cheerful kindergarten cartoon turn and hunt. That is a cheap trick played on the youngest, and its imitators multiply because it sells.

The Christian answer is the true kindergarten. A father teaches by the way and at bedtime; a church nurtures; a home keeps watch. And the prophets give the child a better picture of the future: not mascots that become monsters, but beasts that become gentle when the Prince of Peace reigns. Read Isaiah 11 to a child who plays Banban. It is the garden the game cannot imagine.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

German Kindergarten (Froebel, 1837: "children’s garden") → Garten of Banban (Euphoric Brothers, January 2023) → Gen Alpha mascot-horror staple.
